# Smoking Prohibition (Children in Motor Vehicles) (Scotland) Act 2016

The Smoking Prohibition (Children in Motor Vehicles) (Scotland) Act 2016 is an act of the Scottish Parliament which prohibited smoking in a motor vehicle with a child.
Legislative passage
The legislation was supported by the Scottish government and opposition parties in the Scottish Parliament.
Provisions
Those who violate the legislation are subject to a fine of up to  or  if the case goes to court.
Reception
Forest, a smokers' group, described the legislation as patronising.
BMA Scotland supported the legislation.
Further developments
A 2021 study by the University of Glasgow found that asthma hospitalisations fell by 1.49% per month among children under the age of 5 with no effect for children between the ages of 2014 and 2021.
